title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 13
statement: Positive integers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the equation \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} = \sqrt{1183}.\) What is the minimum possible value of \(x + y?\)

solutions.text: Since \(1183 = 7 \cdot 13^2,\) we have \(\sqrt{1183} = 13\sqrt7.\) Squaring the given equation shows that \(\sqrt{xy}\) is rational. Thus \(x\) and \(y\) have the same squarefree part: write \(x=da^2\) and \(y=db^2,\) where \(d\) is squarefree and \(a,b\) are positive integers. Then \((a+b)\sqrt d=13\sqrt7,\) so \(d=7\) and \(a+b=13.\) Therefore \(x+y=7(a^2+b^2),\) which is smallest when \(a\) and \(b\) are as close as possible. Taking \(a=6\) and \(b=7\) gives \(x+y=7(36+49)=595.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Then \(\sqrt{x} = a\sqrt{7}\) and \(\sqrt{y} = b\sqrt{7}\) with \(a + b = 13;\) minimize \(x + y = 7(a^2 + b^2)\)
